newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan spent fuel plant to briefly resume operation.
newsitem.headline: Japan spent fuel plant to briefly resume operation.

text.p: The nuclear fuel reprocessing plant that was shut down last week after a major accident has resumed operations but for only a short while, its operator said on Friday.

A spokesman for the state-run Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) said it had decided to resume operations at one of its main reprocessing facilities because about two tonnes of spent fuel remained inside the unit and needed to be retrieved by completing the necessary process.

All operations at the nuclear reprocessing plant in Tokaimura, Ibaraki Prefecture, were halted on March 11 after a fire broke out at a facility separate from the main units, where nuclear waste is mixed with asphalt for long-term storage.
A PNC spokesman said: "We have decided to temporary resume operations from Friday."
He said the company expected to complete the necessary processing procedure by April 7.
He said the company could not provide a date for a full resumption of operations as it was still investigating the cause of last week's fire.
Significant delays in notifying authorities about a radiation leak from the fire and other lapses in coping with the accident have made the PNC the focus of public criticism.
The PNC also operates Japan's prototype fast-breeder reactor "Monju," which remains closed after an accident in December 1995 involving a massive leak of sodium coolant.
The reprocessing plant is located about 160 km northeast of Tokyo.
